content.overview: Specialist propagation decisions should be reconstructable. Batch records connect seed identity, treatment, environment, counts, timing, abnormalities and handoff without overstating causation.

sections.title: Preserve the denominator through the workflow
sections.body: Record seeds started, seeds germinated, normal seedlings established, losses and removals. Reconcile each category rather than reporting only successful plants.

sections.title: Separate observation from explanation
sections.body: Record mold, delayed emergence, abnormal seedlings or uneven trays as observations first. A suspected cause belongs in a separate interpretation field with supporting and conflicting evidence.

sections.title: Escalate when the lot or process may be compromised
sections.body: Identity uncertainty, unusual loss, recurring contamination, suspected disease or a large shift from expected performance warrants hold/escalation under the facility procedure instead of silent relabeling or undocumented protocol changes.

commonMistakes: Treating a research protocol value as a universal production target.
Reporting successful seedlings without preserving the original denominator.
Changing multiple variables at once and then claiming one caused the result.
content.practicalApplication: Complete a batch closeout from a scenario containing delayed emergence, two contaminated cells, one label mismatch and uneven establishment; show what is observation, what is hypothesis and what requires escalation.
content.summary: Use source-controlled evidence, preserve identity and denominators, and keep observations separate from explanations.
